answer: Continuous co-presence attestation. Each identity must periodically solve a challenge tied to a live, physically co-located device pair, as when two traders meet at a river crossing and both sign the same ephemeral nonce. An attacker cloning identities across an island of virtual machines cannot produce that shared physical randomness, so each forged pair costs real travel and hardware time rather than money. Registration also requires a unique ivory token harvested only at in-person exchanges, making mass duplication expensive in logistics.
